clue.text: Reject is protected by soft feathers

indicators.note: something protected is wrapped round by its guard, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: down is the fine soft plumage of birds
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rejected item lies cushioned in a bed of soft feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: Down here is the noun for soft plumage, not the direction; 'protected by' puts the small word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to refuse to acknowledge them, a synonym for rejecting them.

clue.text: Choose bag for one of Fagin's lot

parts.note: to pick is to choose
to bag something is to pocket it

explanation.surface: An instruction to select a handbag suitable for one of Dickens's young thieves.
explanation.walkthrough: Fagin, in Dickens's Oliver Twist, runs a gang of boy thieves who pick pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Fagin's boys, such as the Artful Dodger, are trained street thieves who steal from pockets.

clue.text: Vigorous, ethical movement takes time

indicators.note: movement suggests the letters are shifted about into a fresh order
takes means the word gains an extra piece added to it

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A vigorous campaign for ethical behaviour needs time to take hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic describes someone strong, fit and energetic, a close synonym for vigorous.

clue.text: Large flag for an Egyptian god

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
a flag is a kind of iris, the plant

explanation.surface: A big banner is made to honour a deity of ancient Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' looks like a banner, but here it is the yellow flag iris, a water plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris was the ancient Egyptian deity of the underworld and resurrection.

clue.text: Offering absolution somehow, leaving us out

indicators.note: somehow says the remaining letters are arranged in some other way
leaving out means those two letters are dropped from the longer word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A priest offers forgiveness of sins in some fashion, but not to us.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove U and S from ABSOLUTION, then rearrange ABOLTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblation is a religious offering presented to God or a deity.

clue.text: Impudent but fashionable channel

parts.note: in means in fashion
the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England

explanation.surface: A cheeky but trendy TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is a stretch of sea off southern England, a sailing hotspot.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent and impudent are synonyms for rudely disrespectful behaviour.

clue.text: Inept act rendering little reward

indicators.note: rendering means translating or remaking, so the letters come out in a new form

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A clumsy performance earns the actor only a small fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A pittance is a very small or inadequate amount of money paid to someone.

clue.text: Anorak expert?

parts.note: surface reading: a specialist in waterproof hooded jackets
setter's reading: an anorak is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast, an expert in some dull niche

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang an anorak is a socially awkward obsessive, like a trainspotter in a hooded coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A socially awkward person obsessed with a specialist subject is exactly what the slang anorak describes.

clue.text: The rose-breasted ibis is found in this area

parts.note: surface padding: the bird only sets the scene

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, waiting to be spotted

parts.note: the letters sit in the middle of the second half of this word

explanation.surface: A birdwatching note on where a pink-chested ibis lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'this area', the region the clue's own wording points to.
explanation.definitionFit: The East is a compass region of the world, an area such as Asia.

clue.text: Large noise about injury

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A loud din has caused someone harm.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesion is a wound or area of damaged tissue, a medical term for an injury.

clue.text: Heavenly antics for fliers

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as ..., pranks up in the heavens
second meaning: songbirds famous for singing in flight

explanation.surface: Aerial stunts put on for pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a prank, so sky larks are antics in the sky; skylarks are also small birds that sing high aloft.

clue.text: Latest count rectified for recruiting agent

indicators.note: rectified means corrected or put right, so the letters are put into a proper order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The most recent tally has been corrected for an employment agency.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent scout searches for gifted people to sign, for example to a sports club or record label.

clue.text: Healthy compound of Oasis, Blur and UB40, originally

indicators.note: a compound is a mixture, so the letters are blended together anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: originally points to the very start of the band name

parts.note: the first character of the band name

explanation.surface: A wholesome blend of three British pop bands.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasis, Blur and UB40 are British bands; only the first letter of UB40 is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Salubrious means conducive to good health, such as a healthy climate or neighbourhood.

clue.text: Moodiness, sadly, when one son leaves the game

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are disordered
one son leaving means a single letter for son drops out

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for son; it is removed

explanation.surface: A sulk descends when one boy walks out of the family game.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominoes is a game played with small oblong tiles marked with spots.

clue.text: Wealthy one is loud and eloquent

parts.note: a means one
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a fluent speaker is eloquent

explanation.surface: A rich person is noisy and articulate.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluent means having plenty of money, a straightforward synonym for rich.

clue.text: Confess to aim for an unprofitable strike

parts.note: to own up is to confess
a goal is an aim

explanation.surface: Someone admits their purpose in calling a walkout that will cost money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like industrial action, but it is a shot at goal in football.
explanation.definitionFit: In football an own goal is a shot into your own net, a strike that scores for the opposition.

clue.text: Person looking at a newspaper

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a watcher or onlooker
second meaning: The ..., a British Sunday paper

explanation.surface: Someone is reading a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, sister of the Guardian.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker who watches is one sense; the other is the title of a long-running British Sunday paper.

clue.text: Knee-jerk reaction spoiled start

parts.note: a reflex tap below the knee makes the leg kick
food gone off is spoiled

explanation.surface: An impulsive response ruined the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: The kick-off is the opening of a football match, and by extension the beginning of anything.

clue.text: Wealthy locum's beat, turned tail

parts.note: a locum is a sub, a stand-in; with the 's attached

indicators.note: turned suggests the letters are twisted into another arrangement

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-off stand-in doctor took a beating and ran away.
explanation.walkthrough: A locum is a stand-in doctor; 'turned tail' reads as fleeing, but only the last word is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Substantial can mean well-off or prosperous, as in a substantial landowner.

clue.text: Jack left the amphibian to gossip …

indicators.note: left means departed, so that word goes away from the longer name

parts.note: the natterjack is a European toad
taken as written; this is removed

explanation.surface: A man called Jack went off, leaving the frog to chat.
explanation.walkthrough: The natterjack is a toad found in Britain; strip off JACK to leave NATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To natter is a British informal verb for chatting idly, much like gossiping.

clue.text: … that is repeated by 4 across's wife

indicators.note: repeated means the short word is written down twice in a row

parts.note: taken as written, then written out a second time

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, the gossip is passed on by the god's spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses join this to the previous clue's surface; 4 across is OSIRIS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Egyptian mythology Isis was the sister and consort of Osiris.

clue.text: Sailor-scholar in a group

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
BA is a Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A seafaring academic joins a band.
explanation.definitionFit: ABBA was the Swedish pop band that won Eurovision with Waterloo.

clue.text: Bus returning to old city, Fabians' central residential district

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: taken as written, then turned round
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

indicators.note: central asks for just the middle part of that name

parts.note: the middle three letters of the name

explanation.surface: Members of the Fabian Society take the bus back to an ancient city's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fabian Society is a British socialist group; its members are Fabians.
explanation.definitionFit: Suburbia is the collective term for the residential outskirts of a city.

clue.text: Caress causing a seizure

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to pass the hand gently over
second meaning: a sudden attack such as apoplexy

explanation.surface: A gentle touch brings on a fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Stroke is both a gentle sweep of the hand and a sudden brain attack from interrupted blood supply.

clue.text: Fake fuel switch is shocking

parts.note: a sham is a fake

indicators.note: a switch is a change round, so the letters swap places

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Swapping in counterfeit fuel is a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shocking can mean disgraceful, and shameful means bringing disgrace.

clue.text: Flies with alien in a fashionable group

parts.note: to jet is to fly
ET is the film alien; with simply adds him

explanation.surface: Someone travels with an extraterrestrial among a trendy crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are wealthy socialites who fly between glamorous resorts, a fashionable social circle.
